content.text: In the given diagram illustrating quadrilateral ABCD, if the sum of angle B and angle D is 200 degrees, what is the measure of angle A?

\angle A + \angle B = 180^\circ

content.text: In the given diagram of quadrilateral ABCD, where AB equals BD and point E lies on BD with CE measuring the same as CB, if angle ADB is 65 degrees, what would be the measure of angle DCE?

messages.content:
<think>
AB = BD ∧ \triangle ABD \text{ isosceles} \implies \angle BAD = \angle ADB
\angle ADB = 65^\circ \implies \angle BAD = 65^\circ
\angle ABD = 180^\circ - \angle BAD - \angle ADB = 180^\circ - 65^\circ - 65^\circ = 50^\circ
AB \parallel DC \land BD \text{ is a transversal} \implies \angle ABD = \angle BDC
\angle ABD = 50^\circ \implies \angle BDC = 50^\circ
AD \parallel BC \land BD \text{ is a transversal} \implies \angle ADB = \angle DBC
\angle ADB = 65^\circ \implies \angle DBC = 65^\circ
CE = CB \land \triangle CEB \text{ isosceles} \implies \angle CEB = \angle CBE
\angle CBE = \angle DBC = 65^\circ
\angle CEB = 65^\circ
\triangle CEB \implies \angle ECB = 180^\circ - \angle CEB - \angle CBE = 180^\circ - 65^\circ - 65^\circ = 50^\circ
In \parallel ABCD, \angle BCD = \angle BAD = 65^\circ
\angle BCD = \angle ECB + \angle DCE
\angle DCE = \angle BCD - \angle ECB = 65^\circ - 50^\circ = 15^\circ
\angle DCE = 15^\circ

content.text: What is the measure of angle B in quadrilateral ABCD if point E lies on the extension of side DC, AE equals DE, and angle E measures 46 degrees?

Let \angle ADE = \angle DAE = x. Then 2x + 46^\circ = 180^\circ \implies x = 67^\circ
Hence \angle ADE = 67^\circ
Since E lies on the extension of DC, DE \parallel DC \implies \angle ADC = \angle ADE = 67^\circ

67

content.text: What is the measure of angle D in parallelogram ABCD if the sum of angle A and angle C is 120 degrees, as depicted in the diagram?

messages.content:

\angle A + \angle D = 180^\circ
Let \(x = \angle A = \angle C\). Given \(\angle A + \angle C = 120^\circ \implies x + x = 120^\circ \implies 2x = 120^\circ \implies x = 60^\circ\)
\angle D = 180^\circ - \angle A = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ
Thus \(\angle D = 120^\circ\)
</think>
120

content.text: If angle AOC is measured at 130.0 degrees in the figure depicting a set of triangular plates placed on a desktop (with the right-angle vertices coinciding), what is the measure of angle BOD?

\angle AOC = \angle AOB + \angle BOC, \quad \angle BOD = \angle COD - \angle BOC
\angle AOC + \angle BOD = \angle AOB + \angle COD
\angle AOB + \angle COD = 90^\circ + 90^\circ = 180^\circ
\angle AOC + \angle BOD = 180^\circ
\angle AOC = 130.0^\circ

content.text: In the parallelogram ABCD, point E lies on side BC, and the line segment AE is drawn. If AE bisects angle BAD and angle D measures 58 degrees, what is the measure of angle AEC?

\angle BAD = 122^\circ \implies \angle BAE = \angle EAD = \frac{\angle BAD}{2} = 61^\circ
AD \parallel BC, E \in BC, AE \text{ transversal} \implies \angle EAD = \angle AEB = 61^\circ
\angle AEC = 180^\circ - \angle AEB = 180^\circ - 61^\circ = 119^\circ

119
